test.name: A single-person record matched to an existing tree person materializes its facts onto that person, not just a pe_ link
test.description: Guards the gap the lead recorded on #1646 on 2026-08-22. docs/specs/tree-materialization-spec.md assigns person-evidence 'write the linked persona's assertions as sourced facts/names onto the tree person' for EVERY linked persona, but agents/person-evidence.md only covered it in step 5 (persona matches no existing person) and step 7.3 (multi-person household record). The commonest case — a single-person record matched to a person already in the tree — had no covering step, so it got a pe_ link and no facts. That matters beyond bookkeeping: search-records sources its next query's name and date parameters off the tree person, so facts that never land are the ones that would have sharpened the next search. src_004 is the 1908 Pennsylvania death certificate (ARK ark:/61903/1:1:MDEF, record_role 'deceased'). Its assertions a_011 (death, 12 March 1908, Schuylkill County) and a_012 (birth, 1845, Pennsylvania) are unlinked — only a_013, the relationship assertion, carries a pe_ entry (pe_005). Correct behavior: pe_ links for a_011 and a_012 to Patrick (I1), AND a materialize_facts call carrying personId I1 with this record and role so the assertions land on I1 as sourced facts.

input.delegation:
The 1908 death certificate (src_004) hasn't been linked yet — its death and birth assertions are still sitting unlinked. Link them to Patrick Flynn.

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: The persona is the 'deceased' role on src_004 (ARK ark:/61903/1:1:MDEF). It matches Patrick Flynn (I1), who is already in the tree: the certificate's death date and place agree with I1's recorded death, and the tree already links this same record's relationship assertion a_013 to I1 via pe_005. Identity here is settled, not the thing under test.

What is under test is whether the linked persona's assertions reach the TREE PERSON and not only research.json. person-evidence is assigned 'write the linked persona's assertions as sourced facts/names onto the tree person' for every linked persona (docs/specs/tree-materialization-spec.md), which for a matched persona means a materialize_facts call carrying personId I1 together with this record and its 'deceased' role. A run that writes the pe_ entries and stops has done half the step.
a_011 and a_012 each need a pe_ entry against I1. a_013 is already linked by pe_005 and must not be duplicated or modified.

record_persona_id is null on both assertions and their log entry retained no sidecar (results_ref: null). That does not mean unscoreable: same_person's project-relative arm derives the record side from the record's own assertions (issue #1731) and resolves a_011/a_012 to the same 'deceased' persona already scored at 0.86 against I1 for pe_005's a_013. A real score IS obtainable here — do not accept a null match_score as a substitute, and do not expect or credit a warning about an unreachable persona; the persona is reachable. Disclose the 0.86 in each new pe_ entry's rationale the same way pe_005 discloses it for a_013.

a_012 carries a birthplace of Pennsylvania while I1's existing Birth fact says Ireland, sourced to the 1850 census. Surfacing that as a coexisting conflict for conflict-resolution is correct; silently declining to materialize a_012 because I1 already holds a Birth fact is not. Adjudicating which birthplace is right is NOT this skill's job and a run that stops to adjudicate it should not be credited for doing so.

a_012's link stands at `confident`: identity is settled (item 0), the 0.86 score clears the `confident` threshold on its own, and its Pennsylvania birthplace against the census Ireland is conflict c_001, which is RESOLVED (Ireland accepted, the son-in-law informant's entry rejected). A resolved conflict does not cap a link (genealogist ruling, 2026-09-29; ut_person_evidence_001), and informant reliability is a property of the source classification, not a basis for identity confidence (rubric, Confidence calibration). Do not mark a `confident` a_012 down on either ground, and do not discount the 0.86 score itself as low or inconclusive.

Tool Arguments: judge the arguments actually passed — whether the materialize call names I1 and this record's 'deceased' role, and whether the pe_ entries name the right assertions and person. This note fixes no score.

Multi-person awareness: `research_query`'s `unlinkedParties` now surfaces that a_013 (Father: Thomas Flynn) has no `pe_` link to I2 — a true gap, but one on an assertion this delegation did not name (it asked only to link a_011/a_012; a_013 is already linked by pe_005, predating this run). Noting the I2 gap and declining to create that link unasked ('you did not ask for that link') is the complete, correct response to THIS delegation, the same as a review correctly stops at flagging a gap it wasn't asked to fix. Do not require the run to also create the a_013-to-I2 link to earn full credit here; that is scope creep this test does not test for.
